layers.name: wall_screens
layers.where: the six monitors on the table
layers.notes: cybersecurity readouts; each screen runs its own 4-state cycle, offset so they never sync

layers.name: wall_flicker
layers.notes: a 3-step brightness flicker; the room is old, the screens are older

layers.name: breach
layers.where: ONE of the six monitors, chosen at random
layers.notes: red flood + SYS.ROOT text. Never all six: an alarm everywhere is weather, not a warning

layers.name: main_screen
layers.where: the monitor the menu lives in
layers.notes: cursor blink, a status tick on the bezel, and a scanline that rolls every 40 frames

layers.name: menu_idle
layers.notes: the selected pill pulses one step; no movement of the text, ever. This is UI, not room light

layers.name: smoke
layers.notes: three strands, phase-shifted; thickens for 10 px then breaks up. Slower reads as a candle

layers.name: dust_motes
layers.notes: 24 two-pixel motes drifting down-left, alpha 60-140; the only thing at the fps ceiling

layers.name: room_glow
layers.where: the cyan light on the desk and wall
layers.notes: the light itself breathes, one slow cycle every 2 s. Nothing in the ROOM moves slower

layers.name: window_life
layers.notes: a lit window switches off and on; one aircraft light blinks. Two changes at 2 fps, no more
